François Bozizé learned while an Army general in the 1970's and '80s what a paradise it could be for the ruthless and cunning. Flash forward to 2001, Bozizé is Chief of Staff of the Army to the new elected president Ange-Félix Patassé. Bozizé crushes several rebellions against Patassé's elected goverment and receives honors and medals. Once the President is out of the country on business in 2003, Bozizé issues a coup and his army takes the capital with the surprise help of troops from Libya and other countries.

Chief of Army Staff François Bozizé Yangouvonda, however, wants a mandate from the people, or the least the appearance of one, and wins an election in 2005, after a special second vote is tallied for reasons not known to many. And so seven years of what amounts to peace in Central Africa passes.

France was asked to help stop the insurrection, but François Hollande refused to intervene. Defeated, Séléka's funding dried up. Djotodia ordered the group disbanded, and new elections were held in 2015. A government offical who was previously an interim Prime Minster named Faustin-Archange Touadéra won the election, and has held power since.
